newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/New tech index draws interest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/New tech index draws interest.

text.p: The newly listed options on Goldman Sachs technology indices drew solid interest Friday as the technology sector continued to outperform the broad market.

The Chicago Board Options Exchange listed seven Goldman Sachs technology indices Friday and big trades crossed in the Goldman Sachs Technology Indexes (GSTI) composite index .GTC and multimedia networking index .GIP.
Two thousand of the GIP October 105 puts traded in two blocks of 1,000. The trades crossed at 2-1/4.
At 1455 CDT (1955 GMT), the October 105 put was bid at 2-3/8 and asked at 2-3/4.
The index was down 1.08 points at 107.42.
On the GTC, 2,000 of the October 105 puts also traded, also in two blocks of 1,000. The trades crossed at two. The option was later bid at 2 and asked at 2-3/86.
"That's quite a bit of size" for such new options, said Jesse Stamer, general partner at TradeNet LP.
He said the trades appeared to be from an institutional investor along the lines of a Fidelity Investments, one of the biggest mutual fund houses in the world.
He said the investor was most likely using the new puts to hedge a portfolio, which is common practice among big institutional investors.
In other trading, PepsiCo Inc options were active on the CBOE as investors reacted to the company's restructuring news announced after the close on Thursday.
At 1455 CDT (1955 GMT), PepsiCo shares were off two at 28-1/4. They had reached a session low of 28-1/8. Volume was about 2.2 million shares.
Among the options, the October 30 call was most active, with about 3,100 contracts changing hands. The January 30 call traded nearly 3,100.
On the put side, the October 30 traded 1,530 contracts, the January 27-1/2s traded about 700 and January 30s nearly 500.

"There seems to be a majority of put sellers and call buyers," said Kevin Hincks, a CBOE market maker. "There have been some call sellers, but it seems the calls they shorted at higher levels, they're covering now at lower levels."
The October 30 call was down 3/4 at 3/8 and the January 30 call was off 15/16 at 1-5/16.
In the November series, the 27-1/2 call, which traded more than 500 contracts, fell 1-1/4 to 1-7/8. The 30 call lost 7/8 to 3/4. More than 700 contracts changed hands.
Hincks said that while most of the PepsiCo business was in the October and January options -- the two series with the highest open interest -- activity was spread throughout all series.

Late Thursday, the food and beverage giant unveiled a major restructuring that included more than $500 million in charges. Early Friday, the company said its 1997 earnings would likely be about $0.10 below current forecasts. --Gregory Crawford, 312-408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
